newsitem.title: India: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 2.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
SIX MORE JOIN GUJRAL CABINET

Prime minister I.K. Gujral expanded his council of ministers, inducting P. Chidambaram, as the finance minister, and three other representatives of the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC). Also sworn in were two from the Janata Dal, including United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy. Reddy, the only new face in the cabinet, was allocated the information and broadcasting portfolio, which was earlier held by C.M. Ibrahim in addition to civil aviation. The five other ministers retained the portfolios they held in the previous government.
Financial Express
SAMSUNG, DAEWOO BID TO WOO GODREJ FOR PRODUCTION TIE-UPS

Samsung and Daewoo were believed to be separately negotiating with Godrej-GE Appliances, India's largest refrigerator maker, for production tie-ups. The Korean rivals were in the process of setting up their own production bases to manufacture refrigerators primarily to cater to the top end of the market. The proposed production tieups with Godrej-GE, their local rival, were meant to ensure ready supplies of refrigerators for the Korean companies in lower price segments.
$1 BLN SYNDICATED LOAN FOR INDIAN OIL CORP

Indian Oil Corporation contracted a fully underwritten, two tranche $1 billion one-year syndicated loan facility to fund oil imports in 1997/98 (March-April). The first tranche of $500 million, inclusive of a $100 million greenshoe option, was contracted at 25.5 basis points over Libor. Dutch banking major ABN Amro was the coordinating arranger for this loan facility along with other banks. Sources said the second tranche of the same amount would be linked to the future rating of the country by international raters.
PETRO PRICE HIKE POSSIBLE TO CHECK OIL POOL DEFICIT

Prime Minister I.K. Gujral hinted at an increase in petroleum prices as the government could not allow the oil pool account to swell. He also expressed concern over the high fiscal deficit of over 500 billion rupees. On the fate of the budget, the prime minister said prior to passing the finance and appropriation bills, an all-party meeting would be called and certain provisions modified, if necessary.
PACKAGE TO ACHIEVE NINTH PLAN POWER CAPACITY TARGET PLANNED

The Power Ministry formulated a package to achieve the Ninth Plan (1997/2002) target of 57,000 megawatts in additional capacity requiring a 2,280 billion rupee investment. The package was formulated in view of serious constraints in the power sector, which in the Eighth Plan (1992/1996) led to a 16,415 megawatt shortfall. The steps being initiated include completion of ongoing projects, ensuring full funding to ongoing projects, higher investments in state owned firms, policy structuring to encourage private investment, encouraging captive, co-generation and private mega projects and greater delegation of powers to states.
Business Standard
FULL TELECOM COMMISSION TO MEET ON MAY 5

The full meeting of the Telecom Commission, the apex body of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), would be held on May 5. The commission would discuss the proposed tie-up between British Telecom and state owned Videsh Sanchar Nigam. It would also discuss the Hughes Ispat request to allow it to hold the Karnataka and Maharashtra basic telecommunication services licences under two separate companies. A full meeting of the commission is convened when important decisions, some of which have a bearing on policy, are to be taken by DoT.
INDIA MAY TAKE SPECIAL 301 LISTING TO WTO

India may take up the issue of being listed on the Special 301 priority watch list bilaterally with the United States. India would also keep open the option of invoking the World Trade Organisation's dispute settlement mechanism to ensure such unilateral measures did not impede trade. The government said the U.S. government's decision was not in consonance with the positive trend in the development of commercial and business relations between the two countries.
GE CAPITAL RAISES OPEN OFFER FOR SRF FINANCE

In a change of plan, GE Capital hiked the initial open offer for SRF Finance from the earlier 20 percent to 34.47 percent. It also roped in three other subsidiaries to act in concert with the main acquirer, GE Capital (Mauritius), in picking up SRF Finance's public shareholding. Although the price per share remained the same, GE's acquisition cost would rise to 373.7 million rupees from 214 million rupees. The company had arranged for the full amount required for the acquisition -- a primary requirement under the new takeover regulations.
ADB TO HOST INDO-BANGLADESH POWER EXCHANGE TALKS

The Asian Development Bank (ADB) will host the first formal direct negotiations between the Bangladesh Power Development Board and the PowerGrid Corporation of India for exchange of power between the two. Considering the politically sensitive nature of the issue, neither India nor Bangladesh thought of holding the dialogue on its territory. ADB, which was keen on the two countries exchanging power in mutual interest, not only agreed to host the initial meetings at its headquarters in Manila, but would also fund the construction of the transmission link.
MOVE TO REVERSE AVIATION POLICY GAINS MOMENTUM

Moves were afoot to make significant changes in the new civil aviation policy as pro-reform ministers asserted themselves under the I.K. Gujral dispensation. The transfer of the civil aviation secretary was being observed as an important move to reverse the ministry's anti-foreign investment stance. Moreover, spiking the Tata-Singapore Airlines joint venture proposal through a policy announcement after the last government lost support, had attracted criticism within the ruling coalition.
The Observer
PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE FOR CHANGES IN CENTRAL EXCISE ACT

The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) asked for amending the Central Excise Act to levy interest on delayed payments arising out of finalisation of provisional assessments. Delays in finalising provisional assessments of excise duty resulted in large amounts of revenue being locked up every year in disputes. The PAC said about 2,157 cases of provisional assessment involving differential duty of 20.8 billion rupees were pending finalisation as on December 31, 1996.
IGFC TO SET UP 18.5 BLN RUPEE PROJECT IN GUJARAT

Indo Gulf Fertilisers and Chemicals Corporation (IGFC), an Aditya Birla group company, will set up a 18.5 billion rupee mega greenfield custom copper smelting and refining complex in Gujarat. The plant, the only one of its kind in this part of the country, would have a capacity of 100,000 tonnes per annum (tpa) of copper with a built in provision for expansion up to 150,000 tpa.
Business Line
NINTH PLAN EXPORT TARGET AT $100 BLN

The Commerce Ministry said the country's export target of $90 billion to $100 billion could be achieved by the end of the Ninth Plan (1997/2002). This would mean doubling the present level of exports within the next five years. India's exports during April-December 1996 were valued at $24.2 billion, a 6.4 percent growth over exports worth $22.7 billion for the same period in 1995.
NORMS MODIFIED FOR FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN NON-BANK FINANCE

The government announced modified guidelines and specific sectors in which foreign direct investment (FDI) in respect of non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) would be allowed. All proposals for foreign equity investment in NBFCs would henceforth be considered by the Foreign Investment Promotion Board. Foreign investment in NBFCs would be permitted in merchant banking, underwriting, portfolio management services, venture capital among others.
